chunks: Muḥammad al-Ḥalabī narrated from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:
"In cases of killing, none is permissible except a man; and in ẓihār and the expiation of an oath, a young boy is permissible."

key_terms.الظِّهَارِ: ẓihār, a pre-Islamic form of marital repudiation that carries expiation
key_terms.الْقَتْلِ: killing; here, the case requiring expiation for homicide
key_terms.الْيَمِينِ: an oath, for which expiation may become due
key_terms.رَجُلٌ: an adult male, considered valid in this legal context
key_terms.صَبِيٌّ: a young boy; here, one deemed permissible in the specified expiatory contexts
key_terms.كَفَّارَةِ: expiation; the prescribed act that remedies a violation

ai.seo_question: Who is permissible in expiation for killing, ẓihār, and oaths according to Imam al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning who is valid for use in expiatory matters. It distinguishes between killing, in which only a man is acceptable, and ẓihār and expiation of oaths, in which a young boy is acceptable.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.4324 - Muhammad al-Halabi narrated from Abu Abdillah (as) who said:
"In cases of murder, only an adult man is permissible for expiation. However, in cases of ẓihar and the expiation of oaths, a young boy is permissible."
